rv.q: I'm glad that it was Boop! as it was well acted and a lot of fun.
BOOP! delivers the kind of Broadway spectacle that can make you forget your everyday troubles for a while.

The story, featuring a book by Bob Martin, music by David Foster and lyrics by Susan Birkenhead, takes a “throw it all at the wall and keep everything that does and doesn’t stick” approach resulting in a musical tale that is somehow both overstuffed and incredibly thin.
Clearly, “Boop! The Musical” is a piece of fluff, lighthearted and fun with a message so marginal it gets lost in the colors of the lights and cotton candy of the show.
I defy you to leave this pleasing musical without a smile on your face or a pep in your step.
Clever play between the 1930s black-and-white cartoon-iverse and a hypersaturated modern-day New York City conjures dazzling scenes.

cn.t: Critics praise "Boop! The Musical" for its dazzling visual spectacle, with particular acclaim for the stunning choreography, spectacular costumes, and magnetic lead performance that bring the Jazz Age icon to vibrant life on stage.
